dedupe_keys.name: large scale oyster reef restoration for coastal protection in brittany climarest

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how the CLIMAREST project tested new reef system designs to restore native European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis) reefs at two pilot sites in Brittany, France, the Rade de Brest and Quiberon Bay. Deployed substrates encourage larval settlement and form large, cohesive oyster aggregates that withstand predation, storms and heatwaves, dissipate wave energy to reduce coastal erosion under sea level rise, and support biodiversity and local fisheries. The flat oyster has declined sharply since the nineteenth century and is now critically endangered and on the OSPAR list. The project ran from 2022 to 2025 with a total budget of about 8.7 million euros, largely from Horizon Europe; the share for Brittany is not given. The page, published in April 2026 and updated in August 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, with links to the CLIMAREST site and a marine restoration toolbox that includes cost-benefit roadmaps. Caveats: long-term funding is not secured, weather caused delays, and coastal protection benefits are expected, not measured. It illustrates nature-based coastal hazard reduction and climate adaptation with living reefs; related records are the Allen Coral Atlas, the Global Mangrove Watch and the Sand Motor case study.
name: Large-scale oyster reef restoration for coastal protection in Brittany (CLIMAREST)
outcomes: Pilot reef structures were deployed at two Brittany sites to form cohesive oyster aggregates for wave attenuation and habitat; upscaling depends on securing long-term funding.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the CLIMAREST Horizon Europe project
